newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ wage index rose 2.9 pct in Sept qtr - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ wage index rose 2.9 pct in Sept qtr - SNZ.

text.p: The purchasing power of wages and salaries, as measured by the Real Wage Rate Index, rose by 2.9 percent in the September 1996 quarter compared with the June quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday.
But SNZ said the rise was entirely due to the effect of the July 1996 tax and benefit changes.
SNZ said tax and benefit changes also largely accounted for the 2.1 percent annual increase in the index.
SNZ said the index would be discontinued.

"This is the last release of the index because of shortcomings which limit the value of the index for both information and analysis, and because of funding constraints within SNZ," Deputy Government Statistician Ian Ewing said.

"The index does not include irregular wage and salary movements such as bonuses and commmissions. It also uses the CPI, which is a household based deflator, and the Labour Cost Index, which is employer-based," he said.
"Neither of these is totally consistent with wage changes which the index is supposed to reflect," he said.
